name: Void Butte
geological_features: A single massive butte formation dominating the tiny world
Impact-shattered terrain on the opposite hemisphere
Fine regolith composed of pulverized rock
description: Void Butte is a tiny, airless body whose most prominent feature is a single massive butte formation that rises disproportionately from its surface. The butte constitutes nearly a quarter of the body's visible profile, a flat-topped column of dense rock that survived whatever cataclysm shaped the rest of the terrain. The opposite hemisphere is shattered and chaotic, evidence of a major impact event.

The surface is utterly still, bathed in the cold light of distant stars. The butte's shadow sweeps across the regolith as the body slowly rotates, the only moving thing on a world where nothing else changes. The gravity is so low that a strong jump could achieve escape velocity, and dust disturbed by footsteps takes hours to settle.

Void Butte is believed to be a fragment of a larger body, torn free by collision and sent tumbling into its current orbit. The butte formation was likely an intrusion of harder rock within the original body, which survived the breakup event intact while the surrounding material shattered. It stands now as a monument to the violence of its own creation.

The body has negligible economic value and lies far from established trade routes. It appears on charts primarily as a navigation hazard, its small size making it easy to overlook. A single automated beacon marks its position, installed after a freighter nearly collided with it during a course correction. Void Butte exists, and that is the most remarkable thing about it.
